items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: We were in some theater playing with Bill Robinson Enwright.

ctx.x: throwing them in the air, and I always said in the present day that no drummer can play drums with the sticks in the air, but it happened then with this fellow in Memphis. Booker Washington, later on he died. He went to New Orleans, then came back to Memphis, and then he went to Chicago, and he passed there from pneumonia or tuberculosis.

Well, me, that man inspired me so much that I didn't want to be nothing but a drummer. I've got some more to tell you later years (inaudible). Why, Lunceford and I had a big argument. We were in some theater playing with Bill Robinson Enwright. This was after we had got to New York and were in the Cotton Club. And we got in a heck of an argument, heated argument. Of course, Lunceford was such a gentleman, he wouldn't dare fight or nothing like that, no -- I was quarterback on his football team and half --…
